The company, the services, the backends and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are on call for observability at Quaymark Shipping, a fictional freight company. Since a config rollout at 13:20, the tracing backend shows almost no new traces. The services say they are sending.
handover: The rollout rotated the backend's API key in the Collector's exporter headers and added a filter processor.
Agent Collectors forward to a gateway Collector, which exports to the backend.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

filtPrompt.title: A filter that drops almost everything
filtPrompt.context: The new filter was meant to drop health-check spans only.

choices.label: Add a debug exporter at detailed verbosity on a copy of the pipeline, see that the condition matches every span (it tests attributes on the wrong level), fix it to match url.path /healthz only, and watch filtered spans fall to the health-check rate

effects.log: The filter now drops only health checks.

choices.feedback: The debug exporter shows exactly what each stage passes on; internal metrics confirm the fix.

choices.label: Remove the filter processor for now
choices.feedback: Spans flow again, including millions of health checks the backend bills for.

choices.label: Restart all Collectors and the services to 'reset' the pipeline
choices.feedback: Restarts change nothing about a wrong filter or a wrong key, and lose the data in flight.

authPrompt.title: 401 from the backend
authPrompt.context: The rotated key in the exporter's headers is wrong.

choices.label: Correct the key in the Kubernetes Secret the header reads from (an environment variable reference), roll the gateway, and confirm sent spans rise and send failures stop
choices.feedback: A 401 is permanent, not retried; fix the credential and confirm in the exporter metrics.

choices.label: Raise retry_on_failure's max elapsed time so spans keep retrying until the key is sorted
choices.feedback: Permanent errors are not retried at all; nothing changes.

choices.label: Paste the new key straight into the ConfigMap's exporter headers

effects.log: The key is pasted into the ConfigMap.

choices.feedback: It works, and the key is now readable by anyone who can read ConfigMaps and in the GitOps repository.

lossPrompt.title: What was lost?
lossPrompt.context: The fraud team asks whether the gap can be filled.

choices.label: Report the gap from the metrics: spans filtered or permanently rejected are gone; add an alert on send_failed_spans and on filtered/accepted ratio, and a persistent queue for transient failures

effects.log: The gap is reported; alerts and a persistent queue are added.

choices.feedback: Permanent errors and filtered spans are dropped by design; alerts on the Collector's own metrics catch the next one in minutes.

choices.label: Report the gap but add no alert
choices.feedback: Honest, but the next gap is found by a human again.

choices.label: Tell the fraud team the Collector will replay the missing spans

effects.log: The fraud team is told the spans will be replayed.

choices.feedback: Dropped spans are gone; the fraud team waits for data that will never come.

reflection.question: Write the incident record: where the spans were lost, how you found each stage, and what will catch it next time.

parts.label: Finding it
parts.criteria: Internal metrics showed accepted, filtered and failed counts per stage; the debug exporter showed the filter's matches; the log showed 401.
parts.modelAnswer: Accepted spans were fine; the filter dropped 99%; the rest failed with a permanent 401. The debug exporter showed the filter matched every span.

parts.label: Fixing and preventing
parts.criteria: Filter fixed and verified, key fixed via the Secret, the gap reported, alerts on Collector metrics.
parts.modelAnswer: The filter now matches /healthz only; the key comes from the Secret; we alert on send failures and the filtered ratio.

scoring.modelReasoning: Debug a Collector pipeline stage by stage with its own telemetry: receiver accepted, processor dropped or filtered, exporter sent and failed counts show where data stops, and a debug exporter shows exactly what a stage passes on. Transient exporter errors are retried from the queue; permanent ones such as 401 are dropped, as are filtered spans, so fix the cause and say plainly what was lost. Credentials belong in Secrets, and alerts on the Collector's own metrics catch the next gap.
